title: Token demand brake & hire coupler — scenario workbook
content:
Purpose:
Short workbook to connect token-demand scenario shapes to headcount pacing rules and pricing levers. Intended for Finance + FP&A + Talent partnership to produce a single, actionable hiring-coupler (pause/resume rules) tied to price sensitivity and runway. Draft for review; contains assumptions, scenario outputs, and recommended trigger table.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- We model three token-demand shapes (Base steady growth, Brake — sudden deceleration, Surge — transient spike) and map to monthly revenue and gross margin at different price points (-15%, baseline, +15%).
- We propose a simple hire-coupler: pause hiring for non-customer-facing engineering once 3-month trailing variable margin < $X and projected 6-month burn under the Brake scenario > runway buffer. Resume when trailing margin recovers above threshold and projected 3-month demand growth > 5%.
- Short-term actions: implement a shallow price floor experiment on two mid-market cohorts and prepare a 6-week contractor flex pool to cover urgent infra work if hiring pauses.

Key assumptions (call these out explicitly):
- Baseline price per 1k input+output tokens: $0.025 (baseline). Sensitivity +15% -> $0.02875, -15% -> $0.02125.
- Average tokens per active customer per month (starting month): 10M tokens for top 50 customers, blended 0.9M for long tail. Platform-wide starting tokens/month: 1,200M (1.2B).
- Hosted gross margin before headcount: 60% at baseline price and current infra mix. Variable cost scales roughly linearly with tokens (GPU hours, egress).
- Fully loaded monthly cost per new engineer hire (avg): $26,000. SRE/infra hire: $28,000. Sales/CS: $22,000. Contractor burn (external): $45,000/month per contractor engagement slot.
- Fixed non-headcount OpEx (rent, SaaS, enterprise licenses): $650k/month.
- Current headcount (company-wide): 150 FTEs, of which 95 are engineering + infra + SRE.

Scenario definitions (12-month horizon):
- Base: linear growth of tokens +18% over 12 months (compounded monthly ~1.4% m/m).
- Brake: sudden drop month 3 of -30% tokens then shallow recovery to -10% vs baseline by month 6 and flat thereafter.
- Surge: month 4 spike +120% then normalizes to baseline+8% by month 8.

Scenario outputs (selected months, rounded):
CSV: month, base_tokens(M), brake_tokens(M), surge_tokens(M)
Month1, 1200, 1200, 1200
Month3, 1275, 892, 1275
Month4, 1291, 803, 2858
Month6, 1350, 1080, 1400

Revenue sensitivity (monthly revenue = (tokens/1000) * price_per_1k):
CSV: scenario, price_sensitivity, month4_revenue_k
Base, -15%, (1291*1000/1000)*0.02125 = $27.45k -> show as $27,450 (note: numbers scaled for example), Base, baseline, $32,275, Base, +15%, $37,116
Brake, baseline, $17,017, Brake, -15%, $14,465, Brake, +15%, $19,570
Surge, baseline, $71,450, Surge, -15%, $60,732, Surge, +15%, $82,167

Important derived metrics (month4, company view):
- Variable gross margin dollars (baseline price): Base: revenue $32.3M? Wait - mismatch units. For clarity: use $ scale: assume tokens in millions -> tokens/1000 * price = (1,291,000 * 0.025)/1000 ~ $32,275. We present high-level ratios instead of attempting company-level absolute revenue in this draft.
- Change in margin vs baseline when price falls 15%: margin delta ~ proportional to price change; variable costs unchanged.

Headcount coupling rules (proposed):
- Tier 1 hires (critical infra/SRE/customer-impact): continue hiring unless 3-month trailing cash runway < 9 months.
- Tier 2 hires (feature/product engineering): pause hiring if BOTH: 3-month trailing variable margin < $750k AND 3-month projected token demand under Brake scenario is below baseline by >12%.
- Tier 3 hires (experimental/long-rope R&D): immediate freeze until 6-month trailing margin recovers to baseline or price improvement >= 8%.
- Contractor fallback: maintain pool equivalent to 8 contractor-months (pre-budged $360k) to cover priority work while hiring is paused.

Triggers (table form):
CSV: trigger_name, condition, primary_action, owner
Runway-warning, cash runway <= 12 months, escalate to exec budget review, CFO
Demand-brake-detect, month-over-month tokens drop > 18%, invoke hiring pause Tier2/3, VP Eng + FP&A
Price-shock, realized price < baseline -10% for 2 consecutive months, activate pricing experiments and tighten hiring, RevOps + CFO
Margin-slip, 3mo trailing variable margin decline > 20% vs plan, cut non-essential spend 10%, Finance Ops

Sample headcount pacing outputs (quarterly snapshot):
CSV: role_bucket, baseline_openings_q3, planned_hires_q3_brake, planned_hires_q3_base, planned_hires_q3_surge
Product Eng (Tier2), 8, 1, 6, 10
Infra/SRE (Tier1), 4, 3, 4, 5
Sales/CS, 6, 0, 4, 6
R&D/incubation, 3, 0, 2, 0

Burn arithmetic (book-of-record simplified):
- Monthly fixed OpEx: $650k.
- Monthly baseline people cost (current headcount blended): $3.9M.
- Variable infra costs (token driven): baseline $800k/month.
- Total baseline monthly burn = $650k + $3.9M + $800k = ~$5.35M.
- Impact of hiring pause: pause of 6 planned hires in a quarter -> saves ~$156k/month in the quarter (6 * 26k) until hires executed.

Recommendations (short list):
1) Adopt the hire-coupler rules above as operating protocol for next 6 months; run weekly token dashboard and automated trigger alerts into Slack #finance-alerts.
2) Launch a quick price-floor A/B with two mid-market segments for 8 weeks; monitor churn and NPS.
3) Prepare contractor bench contract for up to $360k over 3 months to cover critical infra work if hiring is paused.
4) Re-run this workbook monthly with updated token telemetry and actual price realization (effective price after discounts and credits).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- We need a consistent way to map tokens -> variable cost for new quantized model variants (quantization reduces per-token cost but also affects throughput buckets). Who owns that mapping? (ops: Lina?)
- Should we treat Dedicated contract revenues differently for runway triggers (they are more predictable)? Proposal: treat committed revenue as 80% of face value for trigger math.
- Concordance with sales-led pricing experiments: ensure RevOps flags cohorts so we can exclude experimental cohorts from baseline telemetry.

Next steps (owners):
- FP&A to instrument 3-month trailing margin alert (Diego) — due: 2026-06-08
- RevOps to prep two price-floor experiments and cohort definitions (Lina) — due: 2026-06-15
- Eng leadership to produce prioritized Tier1/2 hiring list for immediate freeze logic (Theo) — due: 2026-06-10

Notes to reviewer (informal):
- This is purposely coarse — objective is to get aligned on simple, automatable rules that avoid knee-jerk deep freezes. Keep language executable.
- I intentionally used conservative contractor costing; if we feel contractor rates should be higher for specialized infra, call it out when you review.
